title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
abstract: arXiv:2607.16097v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become central to improving large language models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, yet RL post-training is largely studied in isolation from the pretraining that precedes it. As a result, two basic questions remain open: (1) how do pretraining choices (model size, data) shape the returns to RL compute, and (2) what does RL actually do to the model? These questions are difficult to study in the standard LLM setting: pretraining corpora are vast and uncontrolled, making it hard to attribute behaviors to pretraining versus RL, and systematic compute sweeps across both stages are prohibitively expensive. To address these challenges, we use chess as a controlled testbed for studying reasoning across the full pretraining-to-post-training pipeline. translated_title: 理解从预训练到后训练的推理
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）已成为提升大型语言模型（LLM）在复杂推理任务上表现的核心手段，然而RL后训练通常是与之前的预训练割裂开来研究的。因此，两个基本问题仍然悬而未决：(1) 预训练选择（模型规模、数据）如何影响RL计算投入的回报？(2) RL究竟对模型做了什么？在标准的LLM研究设定下，这些问题难以探究：预训练语料庞大且不可控，难以将模型行为归因于预训练还是RL，而且跨两个阶段进行系统性的计算扫描成本高昂到令人却步。为应对这些挑战，我们采用国际象棋作为受控测试平台，在完整的预训练到后训练流程中研究推理能力。我们遵循标准的LLM训练流程，在人类棋局上预训练从5M到1B参数的语言模型，并在合成……（摘要在此处截断，内容不完整）
tldr: 该论文以国际象棋作为受控测试平台，首次在完整的预训练到后训练流程中系统研究预训练选择（模型规模与数据）如何影响RL计算投入的回报，以及RL后训练究竟对模型的推理能力产生了什么作用。
en_tdlr: Using chess as a controlled testbed, this paper systematically studies, across the full pretraining-to-post-training pipeline, how pretraining choices (model size and data) shape the returns to RL compute and what RL actually does to the model's reasoning ability.
